about: Box-seconds per group of the proof lane (proof/checks/sharding.py), for each profile (proof/lane/readers.py: readers, the nightly's, every state served to the readers; no-readers, the pull request lane's, PROOF_READERS=0): a group's seconds on one worker, without what the worker's session shares, divided by the workers sharing a CI box. Each profile's execution is CI's default shard count, runner and workers per shard for it. Refresh a profile from its runs: node proof/run.mjs --timings <output directory>... [--box-workers n].

execution.basis: execution.budget: the seconds a shard of a lane with the readers is expected to run at most (python3 -m proof.lane.plan size), three hours. Set from the whole lane with every reader run at head dd12db6b on the proof machines (2026-10-13, 471 groups, 2,053,913 worker-seconds as run): the longest document took 15,711 s on one worker, so its heavier configuration is counted at 10,212 s (0.65 of it, proof.checks.sharding.PIECE_SHARE) and fits the budget with its judging; at 1.7 times, the spread one document's seconds showed between a hosted runner and a proof machine, it is 17,361 s, inside the 345-minute deadline (20,700 s). execution.split: the seconds of one worker past which an observed document or control is queued in pieces, one configuration a worker (python3 -m proof.store.queue), half the budget, so no document queued whole takes more than half a shard: 153 of that run's 441 documents and controls ran past it, 146 as this profile's groups count them. execution.judged: the share of a document's whole measure its judging costs where no run measured that alone; case-list-inline's judging took 8.7 s of 5,871 and connect-deliver-default's 2.4 s of 2,292 with every reader, counted here at five in a thousand.

measured.basis: Worker-seconds of one run of the whole lane with every reader on 2026-10-13, every group observed afresh with no store, as sixteen static bins, each divided by 4, the workers a CI shard's box holds. Eight bins ran on a 96-vCPU proof machine at 88 workers with nothing else on it (0.92 workers a vCPU, the nearest this run came to a CI shard's four workers on four vCPUs) and are kept as measured. Eight ran on a 128-vCPU machine that other runs loaded unevenly, and each of those bins' seconds are scaled to the first machine's density: by the first machine's measured seconds over one set of estimates for its documents and controls (1.229), over the bin's own (factors 0.78 to 0.84 for five bins that ran under load, 1.16 to 1.39 for three that ran nearly alone).

execution.basis: execution.shards: the most shards python3 -m proof.lane.plan fit gives the pull request lane, and its count where a dispatch asks for the default; execution.slots: when each runner the account's twenty-job limit leaves for a shard frees, in seconds after the workflow starts, from pull request run 38081646423's jobs, none earlier than a shard can start, 110: the plan waits for the corpus job, which ends when the main queue is uploaded (88 and 96 seconds into runs 38081646423 and 38425969767, in the job that then held those steps), and the plan's own ten seconds and the few seconds before each job starts follow; execution.fixed: what each shard spends beside its blocks, the pull and setup (75), the lane's start and collection (20), each worker's own Elasticsearch and its first build's wait on the shard's one validation Formplayer (45, 11 less than when each worker started its own, measured on four vCPUs) and the upload (6); execution.gate: the gate job after the last shard.

measured.basis: Observed group seconds from all 15 no-readers shards of GitHub Actions run 39126473734, attempt 1, at df38e762ebeff7945771be61356006aa74bfa47e on 2026-10-18. Each worker record names 4 workers per CI box; refreshTimings divides by that count and averages repeated measurements. All 504 current no-readers groups were measured, including the 19 additions since the prior profile. The run completed its observations but its gate reported failing judgments; these values record elapsed work, not a passing verdict. Other profiles retain their earlier measurements.
